info.name: Ascend API
info.description: Full Ascend backend API, organized into two independent top-level folders: **App (Mobile - Airman)** for the ascend-app Expo mobile app - organized by its real tab bar (Home/Trends/Support/Profile + pre-tab Auth/Onboarding), each tab broken down into its real sub-screens - and **Admin & Provider Dashboards** for the ascend-admin staff web app - organized by role (Admin/Leadership/SCS/PT-IM/Mental Performance/Nutritionist/Chaplain/IDMT), each role's folder broken down by that role's real sidebar tabs. Each top-level folder manages its own auth tokens (app_* vs admin_*). Test accounts: dash-<role>@ascend.mil / AscendDash!2026 for every staff role, dash-airman@ascend.mil for the App side.

request.description: ascend-app has its own local src/app/onboarding/questions.json today - this is the real backend equivalent it should call instead, so option labels/follow_up rules stay server-controlled.

Q3, Q16, Q17, Q18, Q19, Q20 each define a follow_up block (check the Questions response's `follow_up.trigger_options`). If the selected answer is in trigger_options, follow_up_answer is REQUIRED or you get a 400 - correct backend validation. Repeat for all 20 question_ids before Baseline complete succeeds.

item.name: Support tab

request.description: Multipart form, not JSON - optional file attachment. Leave 'file' empty to send without one. Requires a real TeamAssignment link between sender and recipient or this 403s (correct behavior, not a bug). A blocked send (added 2026-08-24) now returns a real severity (1-5, see OPSEC_TERM_SEVERITY in app/core/notification_rules.py) and writes a real message_blocked_opsec audit entry - previously blocked attempts left no audit trail at all. Every severity still blocks the send (this did not loosen the existing behavior) - severity is real added metadata for audit granularity, matching the mobile app's own 'Level 5 (highest) never routes through messaging' description, which had no backing before this.
Response now includes a real severity (1-5, null if no terms matched) alongside blocked_terms - added 2026-08-24.
pathway_key must be one of the `key` values from the Pathways response (e.g. SCS, PT/IM, Nutritionist, Mental Performance, Chaplain).

item.name: Profile tab

request.description: full_name/rank_grade/theme_preference/notifications_enabled are all self-editable, all optional (only send what changed). role and unit_id are deliberately absent here - those stay admin/provisioning-set, a self-service edit of either would be a real authorization/assignment risk, not a cosmetic preference.

Signed-in self-service change - proves intent with the current password rather than an emailed code (that's the separate /auth/forgot-password flow, for when you're locked out). New password needs 8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number, and must differ from the current one. Neither password is ever written to the audit log.

Requires the current password (same 'prove intent' pattern as Change password), since email doubles as the login identifier. On success, is_verified resets to false and a fresh verification code is emailed to the NEW address via the real Resend integration - the old code/expiry were only ever valid for the old address. 400s on a wrong password or a colliding email.

JPG/PNG/HEIC only, 5 MB cap. Not DOCX-sourced (DOCX never asks for a profile photo, and its OPSEC section actively restricts photo uploads) - built as explicit real new scope after a direct ask. Reuses the same encrypted-at-rest FileStorageService as medical records and message attachments, in its own 'avatars' namespace.
document_type: labs|imaging|specialist|dme|other. access_reason min 12 chars.
Same real endpoint as Uploads - add-record.tsx and uploads.tsx are two entry points to the same real upload action.

activity_type must be one of: strength, cardio, mobility, recovery, other (custom_title required if 'other'). intensity is RPE 1-5 (an integer), not a text label. workout-saved.tsx is just a confirmation screen after this succeeds - no endpoint of its own.

OFT (profile/oft.tsx - same real endpoint as Home's)

item.description: Route profile. Identity/settings/sign-out plus the largest sub-screen group in the app - records, uploads, workouts, fly-away kit, data-use, activation.

Organized to match ascend-app's REAL tab bar (src/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx: Home, Trends, Support, Profile + a Check-in redirect button) and each tab's real sub-screens, not a generic backend-module grouping. ascend-app is currently 100% mock/local (confirmed - its baseApi.ts RTK Query shell has zero injected endpoints, no fetch/axios call exists anywhere) - every request here is the real backend endpoint that screen should be wired to, not something already connected. Uses app_access_token/app_refresh_token. Run order for a fresh flow: Auth -> Onboarding (in order) -> Home tab -> everything else.

New password needs 8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number, and must differ from the current one. This is what lets an admin-provisioned user take ownership of the initial password an admin handed them - neither password is ever written to the audit log.
Same current-password-gated pattern as Change password. On success is_verified resets to false and a fresh verification code is emailed to the NEW address.
JPG/PNG/HEIC only, 5 MB cap. Not DOCX-sourced - built as explicit real new scope after a direct ask, since no profile-photo concept exists in the requirements at all.

item.name: Admin

request.description: Backs the 'Add person' modal. Omit initial_password and the server generates one - it comes back once in the response as `initial_password` (share it directly, it is never emailed and never written to the audit log). Send an explicit initial_password to choose your own (8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number). Only a Superadmin can create a DWS Admin/DWS Superadmin account; a plain Admin gets 403 for those but can create every other role.

Backs the People table. Each row carries name/email/role/unit_id/is_active plus `last_edit_at` (the Last edit column) and `created_at`. `last_edit_at` is derived from the audit log - the most recent real account mutation (provisioned/role changed/unit assigned/access renewed/password reset or changed/deactivation requested) - deliberately NOT User.updated_at, which also moves on an ordinary login or check-in. It is null for an account that has genuinely never been administratively edited; use `created_at` as the fallback there rather than showing an invented date.

item.name: Reset password (emails temp password, never returns it)

request.description: Backs the Role catalog table. Per row: role, cluster (the CATEGORY column - Staff | Contractor | Officer | System, matching the screen's own filter buttons), scope, member_count (the ASSIGNED column - real live counts from the users collection, not mock numbers), last_edit (the most recent of that role's real role_changed OR user_provisioned events - both count as a real edit to the role's history, since POST /admin/users can grant a role at creation with no role_changed event at all), and audit_entry_count. `cluster` and `scope` are display-only labels and are never consulted for an access decision - real scoping lives in RoleScopeConfig (cohort_k / visible_components) and each route's require_roles(...). The `Plan` row carries is_real_role: false with honest zero counts: it renders because the design lists it, but Plan is not in SUPPORTED_ROLES so nobody can hold it. Every other row is is_real_role: true. DWS Superadmin is returned too even though the design folds it into ADMIN.

Backs the Roles & RBAC 'Accounts & onboarding' card's 6 metrics. account_status is real is_active/access_expires_at counts. onboarding.in_flight_count is scoped to Airman only (ROLE_PERMISSIONS grants complete_onboarding exclusively to Airman - a staff/admin account's onboarding_status sits at its model default forever since the concept never applies to it; counting every role inflated this from 65 to 116/117 before the scoping fix). onboarding.awaiting_role_confirmation_count is a real PendingConfirmation(action_type=role_change, status=pending) count, cross-checked against GET /admin/confirmations. access_expiration reuses the same real counts as the System dashboard, plus an explicit renewal_note: the mock's screen text claims scopes 'renew automatically on annual review', but app/models/user.py documents access_expires_at is never auto-renewed by any background process - renewal is the existing manual POST /admin/users/{id}/renew-access action, kept honest here rather than matching the mock's false claim. assigned_providers is the real always_available pathway list (SCS + PT/IM). effective_permissions is a reference note pointing at GET /roles/matrix, no new computation. purpose_consent reuses the existing Chaplain/Purpose pathway toggle summary.

9 capability rows x the screen's 10 display columns. Cell states: full | conditional | gated | none. IMPORTANT: `matrix[].roles` is the DECLARED policy transcribed from the design - it is what the screen renders, and it deliberately does NOT always equal what the API actually permits. Each row also carries `enforced` (what that capability's real route gate produces) and the response carries a top-level `divergences` array listing every cell where the two disagree, so the difference is inspectable rather than hidden. Never make an access decision from `roles`; the real route gates are the authority. The PLAN column is display-only - `Plan` is intentionally not a real role (not in SUPPORTED_ROLES, no permissions, no dashboard, no DOCX requirement), so its `enforced` value is `unenforced` and nobody can hold it.

Real 46-question registry: 20 onboarding (O1-O20) + 6 daily (D1-D6) + 10 weekly (W1-W10) + 10 monthly (M1-M10). Fixed 2026-08-23: originally summed to 40 because the daily check-in bank (app/core/checkin_question_bank.py, live-wired into CheckinService) was left out entirely - its questions are literally labeled D1-D6, not a fabricated 'Driver' bank as first assumed. Each row carries readiness_component, routing (derived from the same component ownership used elsewhere), and direction ('Higher = better' / 'Lower = better') - direction is real for every row, derived the same way the live scoring engine derives it (question.get('reverse_scored', False); every one of the 46 real questions is currently False, so every row is genuinely 'Higher = better' today). current_version is the real active QuestionBankVersion (see below), or null if an Admin has never recorded one - never fabricated. No per-question validation_status field - see Question Bank Version below for the real, whole-bank-level equivalent.

DOCX Table 22 'Question Bank Version' entity - version_id/effective_date/retired_date/approved_by/onboarding_daily_weekly_monthly_question_set_id/change_reason. Real whole-bank approval/version record, built 2026-08-23 after re-checking the Contract Question Registry against the DOCX data dictionary - there is no per-question validation concept anywhere, only this whole-bank one, and it had no model/endpoint until now. approved_by is set server-side from the real caller. The active version (surfaced as current_version on GET /admin/question-registry) is the most recent one whose effective_date is today or earlier and is not yet retired - same effective-dating pattern as Scoring Configuration, plus the real retired_date gate that entity doesn't have. Audit logs question_bank_version_created.

Sets retired_date to today - explicit action, not an automatic side effect of recording a newer version (DOCX: 'without breaking scoring history'). 400 if already retired. Audit logs question_bank_version_retired.

Real staffing/opt-in counts for the 3 optional pathways (Nutritionist, Mental Performance, Chaplain), merged with each one's real approval object (built 2026-08-23: the mock's APPROVAL/ENABLEMENT/ACCESS DATES columns were literally the same 3 hardcoded strings copy-pasted across every row in ascend-admin - no DOCX grounding, no backend field. Built as real new scope per explicit instruction, same category as PendingConfirmation). approval.status is 'pending' until an Admin calls approve, then 'approved', then 'enabled' - honest defaults, never fabricated dates.
Admin/Superadmin approves one of the 3 optional pathways. SCS/PT-IM (always_available) 400 - they never go through approval. Audit logs pathway_approved.

400 if the pathway hasn't been approved yet. access_policy is optional free text (matches the mock's ACCESS DATES column, but admin-entered real text, not an invented date). Audit logs pathway_enabled.

Backs the Audit log screen's 4 quick-metric cards. count_24h/count_7d/percent_vs_7d_avg were already real; destructive_action_total_count/_pending_review_count added 2026-08-23 - this method's own docstring already promised a 'destructive-action snapshot' that the code never actually returned (caught re-checking the live 'Destructive actions' card). Sourced from PendingConfirmation, whose own docstring literally calls itself the 'confirmation queue for destructive admin actions' - every action type it tracks counts (role_change/deactivation/export/idmt_handoff), not a narrowed subset.

Backs the 'X required contract reports' panel - real, DOCX-verbatim this time, not fabricated like the rest of that panel's columns. DOCX Table 26 ('Report | Required Sections | Primary Users') names exactly 9 reports; this endpoint's docx_name/required_sections/primary_users are transcribed directly from it. Built 2026-08-23 realigning the report catalog: 3 of the 9 (idmt_handoff_summary/medical_records_audit/performance_summary_export) had no builder anywhere before this - all 3 restricted-sensitivity, added to REPORT_BUILDERS in both places it's defined (admin/routes.py and scheduled_export_service.py - kept in sync). A 4th, leadership_aggregate_readiness, replaces the pre-existing wing_weekly_ops/monthly_cohort_review/annual_wing_readiness (all 3 explicitly 'not DOCX-sourced', each narrower) with a real composite matching DOCX's actual required sections (OPS trend, reconditioning status, utilization summary, equipment gaps - 'recommendations' omitted, no real aggregate data source for it). last_generated_at/last_export_status are real, derived from the most recent actual ReportExport for that report_type - null/never for one that's never been generated. No due date, no named approver, no 'CUI' label - none of those have any real backing anywhere, unlike the report list itself.

recipient_role added 2026-08-23 (now required) - a real DOCX Data Dictionary field on the ReportExport this schedule eventually creates (Report | ...recipient_role...), previously only ever defaulted to the generating admin's own role for on-demand exports. sensitivity_level is NOT client-supplied - computed once at creation from REPORT_SENSITIVITY (the same real aggregate/controlled/restricted gating already used for on-demand exports and the scheduler's own restricted-export second-reviewer check), not the mock's free-text 'Scope' field, which would have duplicated that gating with a second, driftable copy. Live-verified end to end: an aggregate report_type derives sensitivity_level='aggregate', a restricted one derives 'restricted', and when the scheduler actually executes a due schedule the resulting real ReportExport row carries the schedule's recipient_role through on both the plain-export and the restricted/PendingConfirmation paths.

Extended 2026-08-23 - previously status-only (pause/resume). Backs the Exports 'Schedules' table's Edit action, which had no real support beyond pause/resume. Only the fields given are changed - omit any field to leave it as-is, so {"status": "paused"} still works exactly as before. report_type (and therefore sensitivity_level) is deliberately never editable, matching the design's own Edit wizard, which never re-asks for it either. Changing cadence recomputes next_run_at from now, same as at creation. Audit-logs scheduled_export_updated (or _paused/_resumed if status is the only field changing) with an old->new diff per field. Live-verified: a 4-field edit correctly updated all 4 and recomputed next_run_at; invalid cadence/export_format correctly 400; an empty body correctly no-ops without writing a spurious audit entry.

report_type: injury | assessment_completion | utilization | prs_qcp | audit_log | oft_metrics | wing_weekly_ops | monthly_cohort_review | annual_wing_readiness | leadership_aggregate_readiness | idmt_handoff_summary | medical_records_audit | performance_summary_export. The last 4 + leadership_aggregate_readiness added 2026-08-23 realigning the catalog against DOCX Table 26's real 9 required reports - see 'Required contract reports' above.
'restricted' reports (injury, audit_log, idmt_handoff_summary, medical_records_audit, performance_summary_export) return 202 pending-approval instead of the file - approve via Confirmations below.

Each entry now carries a real file_size_bytes (added 2026-08-23) - the Exports 'Recent exports' panel showed a size in MB with no backing anywhere (hardcoded per-row in ascend-admin). Set only where bytes are actually rendered: immediately for a plain/aggregate export (len(content_bytes) at creation, live-verified: 526 for a real wing_weekly_ops CSV, matching the download's real Content-Length exactly). For a restricted export it's honestly null while pending_approval - the real size genuinely isn't known until the first real download materializes it (live-verified: null before approval, 953 after downloading a real approved injury export, again matching Content-Length exactly). Never estimated - doesn't conflict with the download route's 'no sensitive bytes stored at rest' design, since only the byte count is persisted.
lifecycle_status: draft | ready | sent | archived | in_review

Each confirmation now carries a real scope_summary (added 2026-08-23) - a Figma 'Review Pending Request' modal showed a SCOPE field with no backing anywhere (hardcoded per-row in ascend-admin's admin-store.ts). Computed once at request time from already-real data, same pattern as target_summary/consequence_summary: role_change/deactivation use the affected user's real role + unit_id ('SCS - no unit'), idmt_handoff uses its real content_category + target role ('reconditioning - Airman'), export uses sensitivity_level + recipient_role ('restricted - DWS Superadmin'). Live-verified real values for all 4 action types. Note: the same mock's RISK CODE ('Level L4') is deliberately NOT matched - app/services/report_export_service.py already documents choosing non-L-prefixed risk tiers (low/elevated/high) specifically to avoid colliding with this system's real, differently-meaning L0-L5 clinical routing-escalation levels.

item.name: System diagnostics (DB ping, scheduler, AI config)

request.description: active_sessions/pending_transmission_count/threshold_rules.confidence_rule added 2026-08-23, closing 2 of the System screen's real gaps. active_sessions is NOT a real session store (this app is stateless-JWT, no server-side session table) - it's a real, explicitly-labeled proxy: users whose real last_login_at falls within the last 30 minutes (our own inference, no design/DOCX source defines 'active session'), broken into staff/admin/imt. Live-verified it changes with real logins, not static. pending_transmission_count is real, not inferred - IdmtHandoff already tracks a real approved -> transmitted state transition (DOCX Section 8.5); this counts handoffs sitting in 'approved' with no transmitted_date yet. Live-verified reactive: approving a real pending IDMT handoff moved this from 0 to 1. confidence_rule is the real categorical logic from calculate_confidence() written out, not the mock's fabricated '>80%' numeric threshold - this system has no percentage confidence concept. Still genuinely unbacked and NOT invented here: 24h uptime %, a backup system, and a 'Compliance - Nd' day-count - none tracked anywhere in this backend.
The 5 weights must sum to 1.0 or this 422s (real validation).

request.description: DOCX: translate uploaded medical history into performance guidance 'without exposing unnecessary raw medical details'. PT/IM or Admin only. Starts at approved_visibility_level 'draft' - while draft, only PT/IM sees any content (Admin included in that restriction, since DOCX Table 23's Admin cell is 'Metadata; content only if approved').

Every caller gets metadata; content fields are scoped to that role's DOCX Table 23 cell. PT/IM 'Yes' = all; SCS 'Approved limits + RTP guidance' = limitations + RTP; Nutritionist 'Relevant nutrition/recovery only'; Mental Performance 'Relevant stress/sleep/recovery only'; Chaplain and Leadership metadata only; the operator sees their own but never the medication/allergy field. A `withheld_fields` array names what was deliberately withheld, so a null is never ambiguous between 'absent' and 'not for you'.

draft | approved | approved_with_medical. The medication_allergy_considerations_if_authorized field stays withheld from everyone until 'approved_with_medical' - the DOCX field name's own '_if_authorized' suffix is the rule. Audit logged.
Restricted-sensitivity - returns 202 pending-approval, needs a different Admin to approve via /admin/confirmations before download.

Multipart form, not JSON - optional file attachment. Leave 'file' empty to send without one. A blocked send (added 2026-08-24) now returns a real severity (1-5, see OPSEC_TERM_SEVERITY in app/core/notification_rules.py) and writes a real message_blocked_opsec audit entry - previously blocked attempts left no audit trail at all. Every severity still blocks the send (this did not loosen the existing behavior) - severity is real added metadata for audit granularity, matching the mobile app's own 'Level 5 (highest) never routes through messaging' description, which had no backing before this.
Response now includes a real severity (1-5, null if no terms matched) alongside blocked_terms - added 2026-08-24.

item.description: Login as dash-idmt@ascend.mil. Not a tabbed dashboard in ascend-admin - IDMT only receives/acknowledges handoffs PT/IM prepares and Admin approves.

Staff-facing surface, organized to match ascend-admin's real per-role sidebar structure: one folder per role, one sub-folder per that role's real sidebar tab/page, containing the real endpoint(s) that page calls. Uses admin_access_token/admin_refresh_token. Log in once via 'Auth (staff login)' with whichever role's credentials you need (dash-<role>@ascend.mil / AscendDash!2026), then work within that role's folder - a 403 means the logged-in account's role doesn't have that permission, not a bug. `Plan` and `mt` pages exist in the frontend but have zero real backend (explicit decision to skip - no DOCX requirement found) so they're not represented here.
